tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the woman complaining about?

options.A: She has not received any letter from the man.
options.B: Her claim has been completely disregarded.
options.C: She has failed to reach the manager again.
options.D: Her house has not been repaired in time.

questions.cn: 女士在抱怨什么？

optionsCn.A: 她没有收到男士寄来的任何信。
optionsCn.B: 她的理赔完全被无视。
optionsCn.C: 她再次没能联系上经理。
optionsCn.D: 她的房子没有被及时修缮。

questions.stem: What is the problem the woman's family encountered?

options.A: Their caravan was washed away by the flood.
options.B: The ground floor of their cottage was flooded.
options.C: Their entire house was destroyed by the flood.
options.D: The roof of their cottage collapsed in the flood.

questions.cn: 女士一家人遇到了什么问题？

optionsCn.A: 他们的拖车被洪水冲走了。
optionsCn.B: 他们小屋的一楼被淹。
optionsCn.C: 他们的整栋房子被洪水摧毁。
optionsCn.D: 他们小屋的屋顶在洪水中塌了。

questions.stem: What has caused the so-called bizarre technical detail, according to the man?

options.A: The woman's failure to pay her house insurance in time.
options.B: The woman's inaccurate description of the whole incident.
options.C: The woman's ignorance of the insurance company's policy.
options.D: The woman's misreading of the insurance company's letter.

questions.cn: 根据男士，是什么造成了所谓的奇怪的技术细节？

optionsCn.A: 女士没有按时缴纳房屋保险。
optionsCn.B: 女士对整个事件的描述不准确。
optionsCn.C: 女士不了解保险公司的政策。
optionsCn.D: 女士误读了保险公司的信。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she will do at the end of the conversation?

options.A: Revise the terms and conditions of the contract.
options.B: Consult her lawyer about the insurance policy.
options.C: Talk to the manager of Safe House Insurance.
options.D: File a lawsuit against the insurance company.

questions.cn: 对话结束时，女士说她要做什么？

optionsCn.A: 修改合同的条件条款。
optionsCn.B: 就保险政策咨询她的律师。
optionsCn.C: 和安全屋保险的经理谈谈。
optionsCn.D: 起诉这家保险公司。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: Good morning, Safe House Insurance.
lines.cn: M：早上好，安全屋保险。

lines.t: M: My name is Paul.
lines.cn: M：我是保罗。

lines.t: M: How can I help you today?
lines.cn: M：今天我能为您做点什么？

lines.t: F: Morning.
lines.cn: F：早上好。

lines.t: F: I wouldn't say that is good from where I am standing.
lines.cn: F：从我目前的处境看，我可说不出这个早上有什么好。

lines.t: F: This is Miss Wilson, and this is the third time I've called this week.
lines.cn: F：我是威尔逊小姐，这是我本周第三次打电话了。

lines.t: F: Since receiving your letter about our insurance claim, I'm getting a little fed up with my calls about my claim being completely disregarded.
lines.cn: F：自从收到你们关于我们理赔的信函后，我对我的理赔电话完全被置之不理越来越受不了了。

lines.t: M: Miss Wilson, thank you for calling back.
lines.cn: M：威尔逊小姐，谢谢您再次来电。

lines.t: M: Can I take some details to help me look at your claim?
lines.cn: M：我能记录一些细节，以便查看您的理赔吗？

lines.t: F: It's Miss May Wilson of 15 South C Road in Cornwall, and the details are that our village was extensively flooded two months ago.
lines.cn: F：我是梅·威尔逊小姐，住康沃尔郡南 C 路 15 号，情况是：两个月前我们村发生了大范围洪灾。

lines.t: F: The entire ground floor of our cottage was submerged in water.
lines.cn: F：我们小屋的整个一楼都被水淹了。

lines.t: F: And five of us have been living in a caravan ever since.
lines.cn: F：从那以后，我们五个人一直住在一辆拖车里。

lines.t: F: You people are still withholding the money we are entitled to over a bizarre technical detail, and it's not acceptable, Paul.
lines.cn: F：你们公司以一个奇怪的技术细节为由，仍然扣着我们应得的钱，这不可接受，保罗。

lines.t: M: Miss Wilson, according to the notes on your account, the bizarre technical detail that you mentioned refers to the fact that you hadn't paid house insurance the month before the incident.
lines.cn: M：威尔逊小姐，根据您账户上的记录，您所说的那个奇怪的技术细节指的是：事发前那个月您没有缴纳房屋保险。

lines.t: F: That money left our account, and now that you should be paying out, you are suddenly saying that you didn't receive it on time.
lines.cn: F：那笔钱已经从我们账户里划走了，现在该你们赔付了，你们却突然说没有按时收到。

lines.t: F: I'm really sceptical about this claim.
lines.cn: F：我真的对这种说法很怀疑。

lines.t: M: The contract does say that any missed payment in a year will affect the terms and conditions of the insurance contract and may affect claims.
lines.cn: M：合同上确实写着：一年内任何一次漏缴都会影响保险合同的条件条款，并可能影响理赔。

lines.t: M: Of course, I can pass you on to my manager to talk to you more about this.
lines.cn: M：当然，我可以把您转给我的经理，就这个问题跟您多谈一些。

lines.t: F: I've already spoken to him, and you can tell him I'm furious now and that your company has a lawsuit on its hands.
lines.cn: F：我已经和他说过了，你可以告诉他我现在怒不可遏，你们公司要吃官司了。

lines.t: F: You will be hearing from my lawyer.
lines.cn: F：我的律师会联系你们的。

lines.t: F: Goodbye.
lines.cn: F：再见。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the speakers from the conversation?

options.A: They are both worried about the negative impact of technology.
options.B: They differ greatly in their knowledge of modern technology.
options.C: They disagree about the future of Al technology.
options.D: They work in different fields of Al technology.

questions.cn: 从对话中关于两位说话人我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们都担心技术的负面影响。
optionsCn.B: 他们对现代技术的了解差异很大。
optionsCn.C: 他们对人工智能技术的未来意见不一。
optionsCn.D: 他们在人工智能技术的不同领域工作。

questions.stem: What will new kinds of jobs be like, according to the woman?

options.A: Stimulating and motivating.
options.B: Simply writing Al software.
options.C: More demanding and requiring special training.
options.D: Less time-consuming and focusing on creation.

questions.cn: 根据女士，新的工作岗位会是什么样的？

optionsCn.A: 刺激且有激励性。
optionsCn.B: 只是编写人工智能软件。
optionsCn.C: 要求更高并需要专门培训。
optionsCn.D: 更省时间并专注于创造。

questions.stem: What is the risk the man anticipates?

options.A: Old people would be taken care of solely by unfeeling robots.
options.B: Humans would be tired of communicating with one another.
options.C: Digital life could replace human civilization.
options.D: There could be jobs nobody wants to do.

questions.cn: 男士预计的风险是什么？

optionsCn.A: 老人将完全由没有感情的机器人照料。
optionsCn.B: 人类会厌倦彼此交流。
optionsCn.C: 数字生命可能取代人类文明。
optionsCn.D: 可能会出现没人想做的工作。

questions.stem: What is the man's concern about AI technology? In this section, you'll hear two passages.

options.A: It will be smarter than human beings.
options.B: Chips will be inserted in human brains.
options.C: It will take away humans' jobs altogether.
options.D: Life will become like a science fiction film.

questions.cn: 男士对人工智能技术的担心是什么？

optionsCn.A: 它会比人类更聪明。
optionsCn.B: 芯片会被植入人脑。
optionsCn.C: 它会彻底夺走人类的工作。
optionsCn.D: 生活会变得像科幻电影。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: How do you feel about the future of artificial intelligence?
lines.cn: M：你对人工智能的未来怎么看？

lines.t: F: Personally, I feel quite optimistic about it.
lines.cn: F：就我个人而言，我对此相当乐观。

lines.t: M: AI?
lines.cn: M：AI？

lines.t: M: I'm not so optimistic, actually.
lines.cn: M：其实我并不那么乐观。

lines.t: M: In fact, it's something we should be concerned about.
lines.cn: M：事实上，这是我们应该担心的事情。

lines.t: F: Well, it will help us humans understand ourselves better.
lines.cn: F：嗯，它会帮助我们人类更好地了解自己。

lines.t: F: And when we have a better understanding of ourselves, we can improve the world.
lines.cn: F：当我们更了解自己时，我们就能改善世界。

lines.t: M: Well, one thing is for sure.
lines.cn: M：嗯，有一点是肯定的。

lines.t: M: Technology is evolving faster than our ability to understand it.
lines.cn: M：技术的进化快于我们理解它的能力。

lines.t: M: And in the future, AI will make jobs kind of pointless.
lines.cn: M：而且将来，人工智能会让工作变得有点没意义。

lines.t: F: I think artificial intelligence will actually help create new kinds of jobs, which would require less of our time, and allow us to be centered on creative tasks.
lines.cn: F：我认为人工智能实际上会帮助创造新型工作，这些工作需要我们投入的时间更少，并让我们能专注于创造性任务。

lines.t: M: I doubt that very much.
lines.cn: M：我很怀疑这一点。

lines.t: M: Probably the last job that will remain will be writing AI software.
lines.cn: M：最后剩下的工作也许是编写人工智能软件。

lines.t: M: And then eventually, AI will just write its own software.
lines.cn: M：而最终，人工智能会自己写自己的软件。

lines.t: M: At that time, we are going to have a lot of jobs which nobody will want to do.
lines.cn: M：到那时，我们会有很多没人愿意做的工作。

lines.t: M: So we'll need artificial intelligence for the robots to take care of the old guys like us.
lines.cn: M：所以我们需要人工智能，好让机器人照顾像我们这样的老人。

lines.t: M: I don't know.
lines.cn: M：我不知道。

lines.t: M: There's a risk that human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life.
lines.cn: M：存在一种风险：人类文明可能被一种更高级的数字生命所取代。

lines.t: M: AI will be able to completely simulate a person in every way possible.
lines.cn: M：人工智能将能够以一切可能的方式完全模拟一个人。

lines.t: M: In fact, some people think we're in a simulation right now.
lines.cn: M：事实上，有人认为我们此刻就处在一场模拟之中。

lines.t: F: That's impossible.
lines.cn: F：那不可能。

lines.t: F: Humans can't even make a mosquito.
lines.cn: F：人类连一只蚊子都造不出来。

lines.t: F: Computers only have chips.
lines.cn: F：计算机只有芯片。

lines.t: F: People have brains, and that's where the wisdom comes from.
lines.cn: F：人有大脑，智慧就来自大脑。

lines.t: M: Once it's fully developed, AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans, as we would be much slower thinkers in comparison.
lines.cn: M：一旦充分发展，人工智能会厌倦与人类交流，因为相比之下我们的思维慢得多。

lines.t: F: I'm not so sure.
lines.cn: F：我不这么肯定。

lines.t: F: A computer is a computer, and a computer is just a toy.
lines.cn: F：计算机就是计算机，计算机只是个玩具。

lines.t: M: Computers can easily communicate incredibly fast.
lines.cn: M：计算机能够以惊人的速度轻松交流。

lines.t: M: So the computer will just get impatient talking to humans.
lines.cn: M：所以计算机和人类说话会变得不耐烦。

lines.t: M: It'll be barely getting any information out.
lines.cn: M：它几乎获取不到任何信息。

lines.t: F: Well, I believe there's a benevolent future with AI.
lines.cn: F：嗯，我相信人工智能会带来一个良善的未来。

lines.t: F: I also think you watch too many science fiction films.
lines.cn: F：我还觉得你科幻片看太多了。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What are people under 30 advised to do to achieve financial security?

options.A: Try to earn as much money as possible.
options.B: Invest shrewdly in lucrative businesses.
options.C: Save one-fifth of their net monthly income.
options.D: Restrain themselves from high-risk investments.

questions.cn: 要实现财务安全，建议 30 岁以下的人怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 设法尽可能多挣钱。
optionsCn.B: 精明地投资高回报生意。
optionsCn.C: 存下税后月收入的五分之一。
optionsCn.D: 克制自己不做高风险投资。

questions.stem: What should people do if they find it difficult to follow the speaker's advice on their financial plan?

options.A: Cut 20% of their daily spending.
options.B: Ask a close friend for advice.
options.C: Try to stick to their initial plan.
options.D: Start by doing something small.

questions.cn: 如果人们难以遵循讲话者关于财务计划的建议，应该怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 削减 20% 的日常开支。
optionsCn.B: 向密友寻求建议。
optionsCn.C: 努力坚持最初的计划。
optionsCn.D: 从小事做起。

questions.stem: What does the speaker think is important for achieving financial security?

options.A: A proper mindset.
options.B: An ambitious plan.
options.C: An optimistic attitude.
options.D: A keen interest.

questions.cn: 讲话者认为实现财务安全重要的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 正确的心态。
optionsCn.B: 雄心勃勃的计划。
optionsCn.C: 乐观的态度。
optionsCn.D: 浓厚的兴趣。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: To achieve financial security, how much you save is always more important than the amount you earn or how shrewdly you invest.
lines.cn: 要获得财务安全，你存多少钱总是比挣多少钱或投资多精明更重要。

lines.t: If you're under 30 years old, your goal should be to save 20% of your monthly income after tax deductions.
lines.cn: 如果你不到 30 岁，你的目标应该是存下税后月收入的 20%。

lines.t: This is irrespective of how much you earn.
lines.cn: 这与挣多少钱无关。

lines.t: Approximately 50% should be reserved for essentials like food and accommodation.
lines.cn: 大约 50% 应留给食物和住房等必需品。

lines.t: The remaining 30% is for recreation and entertainment.
lines.cn: 剩下的 30% 用于娱乐消遣。

lines.t: But for many young people, it'll be difficult to designate such a large proportion of their income for savings.
lines.cn: 但对许多年轻人来说，把这么大比例的收入用于储蓄会很难。

lines.t: If you find it hard to save any money at all, start by cutting all unnecessary spending.
lines.cn: 如果你发现根本存不下钱，那就从削减一切不必要的开支开始。

lines.t: Allocate a tiny amount of 1 or 2 % for savings and gradually increase that amount.
lines.cn: 先划出一小笔 1% 或 2% 用于储蓄，再逐步增加这个数额。

lines.t: Always keep that 20% goal in mind to prevent yourself from becoming complacent.
lines.cn: 要始终把 20% 的目标放在心里，以防自己变得安于现状。

lines.t: It can be challenging to stick to such a strict plan.
lines.cn: 坚持如此严格的计划可能很具挑战性。

lines.t: But if you adopt the right mindset, you should be able to make it work for you.
lines.cn: 但如果你采用正确的心态，你应该能把它变成对自己有效的方法。

lines.t: So what should you be doing with the money that you're saving?
lines.cn: 那么，你存下的钱该怎么用？

lines.t: Some must be kept easily accessible in case you need some cash in an emergency.
lines.cn: 有些必须放在随时可取的地方，以备紧急时需要现金。

lines.t: The largest proportion should be invested in retirement plans, either through your employer or privately.
lines.cn: 最大比例应投资于退休计划，可以通过雇主，也可以私人办理。

lines.t: And you can keep some money for high-risk but potentially lucrative investments.
lines.cn: 你还可以留一部分钱做高风险但可能回报丰厚的投资。

lines.t: Dividends can be reinvested or used to purchase something you like.
lines.cn: 股息可以再投资，或用来购买你喜欢的东西。

lines.t: By following this plan, you should hopefully be able to enjoy your life now and still be financially secure in the future.
lines.cn: 按照这个计划，希望你能享受当下的生活，同时在未来依然财务无忧。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the speaker when she first started her job?

options.A: She found her outfit inappropriate.
options.B: She was uninterested in advertising.
options.C: She often checked herself in a mirror.
options.D: She was unhappy with fashion trends.

questions.cn: 关于刚入职时的讲话者，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 她觉得自己的穿着不合适。
optionsCn.B: 她对广告不感兴趣。
optionsCn.C: 她经常照镜子检查自己。
optionsCn.D: 她对时尚潮流不满意。

questions.stem: Why were uniforms invented, according to the speaker?

options.A: To save the expenses on clothing.
options.B: To keep up with the current trends.
options.C: To meet the expectations of fashion-conscious clients.
options.D: To save the trouble of choosing a unique outfit every day.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，制服为什么被发明出来？

optionsCn.A: 为了节省服装开支。
optionsCn.B: 为了跟上当下潮流。
optionsCn.C: 为了满足注重时尚的客户的期待。
optionsCn.D: 为了省去每天挑选独特穿搭的麻烦。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about looking smarter?

options.A: It boosts one's confidence when looking for employment.
options.B: It matters a lot in jobs involving interaction with others.
options.C: It helps people succeed in whatever they are doing.
options.D: It enhances people's ability to work independently.

questions.cn: 关于穿得更精神，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它能在找工作时提升自信。
optionsCn.B: 在需要与他人互动的工作中它很重要。
optionsCn.C: 它帮助人们在所做的一切中获得成功。
optionsCn.D: 它提升人们独立工作的能力。

questions.stem: What does the speaker advise people to do in an image-obsessed world?

options.A: Design their own uniform to appear unique.
options.B: Fight the ever-changing trends in fashion.
options.C: Do whatever is possible to look smart.
options.D: Wear classic pieces to impress their clients.

questions.cn: 在一个迷恋形象的世界里，讲话者建议人们怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 设计自己的制服以显得独特。
optionsCn.B: 对抗不断变化的时尚潮流。
optionsCn.C: 竭尽所能让自己看起来精神。
optionsCn.D: 穿经典单品来打动客户。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: I work in advertising and I like to keep up with current trends, mainly because I'm aware that we live in an image-obsessed world.
lines.cn: 我在广告业工作，喜欢紧跟当下潮流，主要因为我意识到我们生活在一个迷恋形象的世界里。

lines.t: However, when I first started my job, occasionally I'd catch a glimpse of myself in the lifts and find myself thinking that I looked a total mess.
lines.cn: 然而，刚入职时，我偶尔会在电梯里瞥见自己，然后发现自己心想：我看起来一团糟。

lines.t: Was I being held back by my choice of clothing?
lines.cn: 我的穿衣选择是不是在拖累我？

lines.t: The short answer is yes, especially when clients are quick to judge you on your style rather than your work.
lines.cn: 简短的回答是：是的，尤其是当客户凭你的风格而非你的工作快速对你下判断时。

lines.t: But no one can be unique with their outfit every day.
lines.cn: 但没有人能每天穿得都独一无二。

lines.t: I mean, that's why uniforms were invented.
lines.cn: 我的意思是，这就是制服被发明出来的原因。

lines.t: So, here's what I did.
lines.cn: 所以，我是这么做的。

lines.t: I created my own uniform.
lines.cn: 我创造了自己的“制服”。

lines.t: To do this, I chose an appropriate outfit.
lines.cn: 为此，我选了一套合适的搭配。

lines.t: Then I bought multiple items of the same style in different shades.
lines.cn: 然后我把同一款式的多件单品买下来，换成不同的色调。

lines.t: Now, I never worry about what I'm wearing in the morning, even if I do get a bit tired of just wearing the same classic pieces.
lines.cn: 现在，早上我从不为穿什么发愁，即便我对总是穿那几件经典单品确实有点腻。

lines.t: Overall, when it comes to work, you have to ask yourself, would looking smarter enhance my ability to do my job?
lines.cn: 总体而言，在职场中，你必须问自己：穿得更精神一些，会提升我的工作能力吗？

lines.t: For some, this question may not be an issue at all, especially if you work remotely and rarely see your colleagues or clients face-to-face.
lines.cn: 对某些人来说，这个问题可能根本不成问题，尤其如果你远程办公、很少与同事或客户面对面。

lines.t: But if your job involves interacting with other people, the answer to this is often yes.
lines.cn: 但如果你的工作需要与他人互动，答案往往是肯定的。

lines.t: So, rather than fighting the system, I think we should just do whatever helps us to achieve our goals at work.
lines.cn: 所以，与其对抗这套体系，我认为我们只管做任何有助于达成工作目标的事。

lines.t: If that means playing it safe with your image, then let's face it, it's probably worth it.
lines.cn: 如果那意味着在形象上求稳，那我们就面对现实吧——这大概是值得的。

tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What has prevented Americans' happiness levels from increasing?

options.A: Their failure to accumulate wealth.
options.B: Their obsession with consumption.
options.C: The deterioration of the environment.
options.D: The ever-increasing costs of housing.

questions.cn: 是什么使美国人的幸福水平没有提升？

optionsCn.A: 他们未能积累财富。
optionsCn.B: 他们对消费的痴迷。
optionsCn.C: 环境的恶化。
optionsCn.D: 不断上涨的住房成本。

questions.stem: What things should we possess, according to the speaker?

options.A: Things that we cherish most.
options.B: Things that boost efficiency.
options.C: Things that cost less money.
options.D: Things that are rare to find.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，我们应该拥有什么东西？

optionsCn.A: 我们最珍视的东西。
optionsCn.B: 能提升效率的东西。
optionsCn.C: 花钱更少的东西。
optionsCn.D: 很难找到的东西。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the items in the speaker's home?

options.A: They are mostly durable.
options.B: They are easily disposable.
options.C: They serve multiple purposes.
options.D: They benefit the environment.

questions.cn: 关于讲话者家中的物品，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们大多耐用。
optionsCn.B: 它们很容易丢弃。
optionsCn.C: 它们有多种用途。
optionsCn.D: 它们有利于环境。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: Did you know that Americans have approximately three times the amount of space we had 50 years ago?
lines.cn: 你知道吗，美国人的居住空间约为 50 年前的三倍。

lines.t: Therefore, you'd think we'd have sufficient room for all of our possessions.
lines.cn: 因此，你会以为我们有足够的空间放下所有物品。

lines.t: On the contrary, the personal storage business is now a growing industry.
lines.cn: 恰恰相反，个人仓储业务如今是一个增长的行业。

lines.t: We've got triple the space, but we've become such enthusiastic consumers that we require even more.
lines.cn: 我们的空间变成了三倍，但我们成了如此狂热的消费者，以至于需要更多。

lines.t: This phenomenon has resulted in significant credit card debt, enormous environmental footprints, and perhaps not coincidentally, our happiness levels have failed to increase over the same half-century.
lines.cn: 这一现象导致了巨额信用卡债务、巨大的环境足迹，而且或许并非巧合的是，在这半个世纪里，我们的幸福水平并没有提升。

lines.t: I'm here to suggest an alternative that having less might actually be a preferable decision.
lines.cn: 我在这里想提出另一种选择：拥有更少也许其实是更好的决定。

lines.t: Many of us have experienced at some stage, the pleasure of possessing less.
lines.cn: 我们许多人都在某个阶段体验过拥有更少带来的快乐。

lines.t: I propose that less stuff and less space can not only help you economise, but also simplify your life.
lines.cn: 我认为，更少的物品和更小的空间不仅能帮你省钱，还能简化你的生活。

lines.t: I recently started an innovative project to discover some creative solutions that offered me everything I required.
lines.cn: 我最近启动了一个创新项目，去寻找能为我提供所需一切的创造性解决方案。

lines.t: By purchasing an apartment that was 40 square metres instead of 60, I immediately saved $200 ,000.
lines.cn: 通过购买一套 40 平方米而不是 60 平方米的公寓，我立刻省下了 20 万美元。

lines.t: Smaller space leads to reduced utility bills and also a smaller carbon footprint.
lines.cn: 更小的空间意味着更低的水电账单，也更小的碳足迹。

lines.t: Because it's designed around an edited collection of possessions, limited to my favourite stuff, I'm really excited to live there.
lines.cn: 因为它是围绕一批精选物品设计的——仅限我最爱的东西——我真的会兴奋地住在那里。

lines.t: How can we live more basically?
lines.cn: 我们如何更简单地生活？

lines.t: Firstly, we must ruthlessly cut the unnecessary objects out of our lives.
lines.cn: 首先，我们必须无情地把生活中不必要的物品清除出去。

lines.t: To stem consumption, we should think before we buy and ask ourselves, will it truly make me happier?
lines.cn: 为了遏制消费，我们应在购买前思考，并问自己：它真的会让我更幸福吗？

lines.t: Obviously, we should possess some great stuff, but we want belongings that we're going to love for years.
lines.cn: 显然，我们应该拥有一些好东西，但我们要的是那些我们会爱很多年的物品。

lines.t: Secondly, we require space efficiency.
lines.cn: 其次，我们需要空间效率。

lines.t: We want appliances that are designed for use most of the time, not for occasional use.
lines.cn: 我们要的是为日常使用而非偶尔使用而设计的电器。

lines.t: Why own a six-burner stove when you rarely use even three burners?
lines.cn: 如果你连三个灶眼都很少用齐，为什么要有一台六灶眼的炉灶？

lines.t: Finally, we need multifunctional spaces and housewares.
lines.cn: 最后，我们需要多功能的空间和家居用品。

lines.t: I combined a movable wall with transforming furniture to get more out of my limited space.
lines.cn: 我把可移动的墙和可变形家具结合使用，从我有限的空间里获得更多。

lines.t: Consider my coffee table.
lines.cn: 想想我的咖啡桌。

lines.t: It increases in size to accommodate 10.
lines.cn: 它能变大，容纳十个人。

lines.t: My office is tucked away, easily hidden.
lines.cn: 我的办公区可以收起来，很容易藏起来。

lines.t: My bed simply pops out of the wall.
lines.cn: 我的床就直接从墙里弹出来。

lines.t: For guests, I can relocate the movable wall and utilise the foldable guest beds I installed.
lines.cn: 对于来客，我可以移开可移动的墙，使用我安装的可折叠客床。

lines.t: I'm not saying we should all live in tiny apartments, but consider the benefits of an edited life.
lines.cn: 我不是说我们都该住在小公寓里，而是想一想“精简生活”的好处。

lines.t: When you return home and walk through your front door, take a moment to ask yourselves, could I do with a little live editing?
lines.cn: 当你回家、走进前门时，花点时间问问自己：我能不能把生活精简一点？

lines.t: Would that give me more freedom and more time?
lines.cn: 那会给我更多自由、更多时间吗？

questions.stem: What did a team of scientists find in their study?

options.A: All respondents were afraid of making a high expense claim.
options.B: A number of respondents gave an average answer of 400 miles.
options.C: Most of the respondents got compensated for driving 384 miles.
options.D: Over 10% of the respondents lied about the distance they drove.

questions.cn: 一组科学家在研究中发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 所有受访者都害怕申报高额报销。
optionsCn.B: 若干受访者给出的平均答案是 400 英里。
optionsCn.C: 大多数受访者因开车 384 英里而获得报销。
optionsCn.D: 超过 10% 的受访者虚报了开车里程。

questions.stem: Why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment, according to the researchers?

options.A: They endeavored to actually be honest.
options.B: They wanted to protect their reputation.
options.C: They cared about other people's claims.
options.D: They responded to colleagues' suspicion.

questions.cn: 根据研究者，人们为什么会编造对自己不利的数字？

optionsCn.A: 他们努力真正做到诚实。
optionsCn.B: 他们想保护自己的名声。
optionsCn.C: 他们在意别人的理赔。
optionsCn.D: 他们对同事的怀疑作出反应。

questions.stem: What does the speaker think of the researchers' findings?

options.A: They seem positive.
options.B: They are illustrative.
options.C: They seem intuitive.
options.D: They are conclusive.

questions.cn: 讲话者如何看待研究者的发现？

optionsCn.A: 它们看起来是积极的。
optionsCn.B: 它们具有说明性。
optionsCn.C: 它们符合直觉。
optionsCn.D: 它们是决定性的。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Now, believe it or not, people sometimes lie in order to maintain a good, honest reputation, even if it hurts them to do so.
lines.cn: 信不信由你，人们有时撒谎是为了维护一个诚实的好名声，即使这么做对自己有伤害。

lines.t: At least, this is what a team of scientists is suggesting, with evidence to prove it.
lines.cn: 至少，这是一组科学家在证据支持下提出的观点。

lines.t: Picture this scenario.
lines.cn: 想象这样一个场景。

lines.t: You often drive for work and can be compensated for up to 400 miles per month.
lines.cn: 你因工作经常开车，每月最高可报销 400 英里。

lines.t: Most people at your company drive about 300 miles each month, but this month you drove 400 miles.
lines.cn: 公司里大多数人每月开大约 300 英里，但这个月你开了 400 英里。

lines.t: How many miles do you think you'd claim in your expense report?
lines.cn: 你觉得自己会在报销单上申报多少英里？

lines.t: The scientists asked this exact question as part of the study we're discussing today, with surprising results.
lines.cn: 科学家在我们今天要讨论的这项研究中问的正是这个问题，结果令人惊讶。

lines.t: They found that 12% of respondents reported the distance they drove as less than the actual figure, giving an average answer of 384 miles.
lines.cn: 他们发现，12% 的受访者申报的里程少于实际数字，平均回答是 384 英里。

lines.t: In other words, they lied about the number of miles, even though they would forfeit money they were owed.
lines.cn: 换句话说，他们在英里数上说了谎，尽管这会让他们放弃本应得到的钱。

lines.t: The researchers believe this was to seem honest, with the assumption being that others would be suspicious of a high-expense claim.
lines.cn: 研究者认为这是为了显得诚实，其背后的假设是：别人会怀疑高额报销。

lines.t: But why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment?
lines.cn: 但人们为什么会编造对自己不利的数字？

lines.t: The researchers explain that many people care a great deal about their reputation and how they'll be judged by others.
lines.cn: 研究者解释说，许多人非常在意自己的名声以及别人会怎样评价自己。

lines.t: If they care enough, their concern about appearing honest and not losing the respect of others may be greater than their desire to actually be honest.
lines.cn: 如果他们足够在意，那么对“显得诚实”和“不失去他人尊重”的关切，可能超过他们“真正诚实”的愿望。

lines.t: The researchers assert that the findings suggest that when people obtain very favorable outcomes, they anticipate other people's suspicious reactions and prefer lying and appearing honest to telling the truth and appearing as selfish liars.
lines.cn: 研究者断言，这些发现表明：当人们获得非常有利的结果时，他们会预期别人产生怀疑的反应，于是宁愿撒谎并显得诚实，也不愿讲真话而被视为自私的骗子。

lines.t: So why is this research important?
lines.cn: 那么，这项研究为什么重要？

lines.t: Well, experts generally agree there are two main types of lie, selfish lies and lies that are meant to benefit others.
lines.cn: 嗯，专家们普遍同意谎言主要有两种：利己的谎言和为他人利益的谎言。

lines.t: The first, as you may predict, is for selfish gain, such as submitting a fraudulent claim to an insurance company, while the second involves lying to help others or not offend others.
lines.cn: 如你所料，第一种是为了私利，比如向保险公司提交虚假理赔；第二种则是为了帮助他人或不冒犯他人而说谎。

lines.t: For example, telling a friend whose outfit you don't like that they look great.
lines.cn: 例如，对朋友说“你看起来很棒”，哪怕你并不喜欢那身衣服。

lines.t: But the researchers are suggesting a third type of lying, lying to maintain a good reputation.
lines.cn: 但研究者提出了第三种撒谎：为了维护好名声而撒谎。

lines.t: Now, this hypothesis is new, and some skeptics argue that this isn't a whole new category of lie, but the findings seem intuitive to me.
lines.cn: 这一假说是新的，一些怀疑论者认为这并不是一个全新的谎言类别，但我觉得这些发现是符合直觉的。

lines.t: After all, one of the main motivations for lying is to increase our worth in the eyes of others.
lines.cn: 毕竟，撒谎的主要动机之一，就是提升我们在他人眼中的价值。

lines.t: So it seems highly likely that people will lie to seem honest.
lines.cn: 所以，人们为了显得诚实而撒谎，看来是极有可能的。

options.A: Older people's aversion to new music.

optionsCn.B: 老年人不断变化的音乐品味。

options.B: They can make subtle distinctions about music.

questions.cn: 从社会心理学被研究最多的定律之一，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 青少年敏感得多。
optionsCn.B: 青少年更容易多愁善感。
optionsCn.C: 青少年的记忆更持久。
optionsCn.D: 青少年的情绪更强烈。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Why do old people dislike new music?
lines.cn: 为什么老年人不喜欢新音乐？

lines.t: As I've grown older, I often hear people my age say things like they just don't make good music like they used to.
lines.cn: 随着自己年纪变大，我常听到同龄人说：好音乐再也做不出来了，不像从前那样。

lines.t: Why does this happen?
lines.cn: 为什么会这样？

lines.t: Luckily, psychology can give us some insights into this puzzle.
lines.cn: 幸运的是，心理学能给我们一些洞察这个谜题的视角。

lines.t: Musical tastes begin to crystallize as early as age 13 or 14, and by the time we're in our early 20s, these tastes get locked into place pretty firmly.
lines.cn: 音乐品味早在 13 或 14 岁就开始成形，到二十出头，这些品味就相当牢固地固定下来了。

lines.t: In fact, studies have found that by the time we turn 33, most of us have stopped listening to new music.
lines.cn: 事实上，研究发现，到 33 岁时，我们大多数人已不再听新音乐。

lines.t: Meanwhile, popular songs released when you're in your early teens are likely to remain quite popular among your age group for the rest of your life.
lines.cn: 与此同时，在你十几岁时发行的热门歌曲，很可能在你的年龄段里流行终生。

lines.t: There could be a biological explanation for this, as there's evidence that the brain's ability to make subtle distinctions between different chords, rhythms, and melodies deteriorates with age.
lines.cn: 对此可能有生物学上的解释：有证据表明，大脑对不同和弦、节奏和旋律做细微区分的能力会随年龄衰退。

lines.t: So to older people, newer, less familiar songs might all sound the same.
lines.cn: 所以对老年人来说，较新的、不那么熟悉的歌听起来可能都差不多。

lines.t: But there may be some simpler reasons for older people's aversion to newer music.
lines.cn: 但老年人反感新音乐，可能还有一些更简单的原因。

lines.t: One of the most researched laws of social psychology is something called the mere exposure effect, which in essence means that the more we're exposed to something, the more we tend to like it.
lines.cn: 社会心理学中被研究得最多的定律之一，叫“单纯曝光效应”，其本质是：我们接触某样东西越多，就越倾向于喜欢它。

lines.t: This happens with people we know, the advertisements we see, and the songs we listen to.
lines.cn: 这发生在我们认识的人、看到的广告、以及听的歌曲上。

lines.t: When you're in your early teens, you probably spend a fair amount of time listening to music or watching music videos.
lines.cn: 在你十几岁时，你可能会花不少时间听音乐或看音乐视频。

lines.t: Your favorite songs and artists become familiar, comforting parts of your routine.
lines.cn: 你最喜欢的歌和歌手成了你日常中熟悉而令人安心的部分。

lines.t: For many people over 30, job and family obligations increase.
lines.cn: 对许多 30 岁以上的人来说，工作和家庭的责任增加。

lines.t: So there's less time to spend discovering new music.
lines.cn: 于是花在发现新音乐上的时间变少。

lines.t: Instead, many will simply listen to old, familiar favorites from that period of their lives when they had more free time.
lines.cn: 许多人干脆只听自己人生中那段拥有更多自由时光的岁月里的老歌、熟悉的心头好。

lines.t: Of course, those teen years weren't necessarily carefree.
lines.cn: 当然，少年时代并不一定无忧无虑。

lines.t: They're famously confusing, which is why so many TV shows and movies revolve around high school turmoil.
lines.cn: 那以令人困惑著称，这也是为什么那么多电视节目和电影围绕高中时期的混乱展开。

lines.t: Psychology research has shown that the emotions that we experience as teens seem more intense than those that come later.
lines.cn: 心理学研究表明，我们十几岁时体验到的情绪，似乎比之后出现的更强烈。

lines.t: And we also know that intense emotions are associated with stronger memories and preferences.
lines.cn: 我们也知道，强烈的情绪与更牢固的记忆和偏好相关。

lines.t: Both of these might explain why the songs we listen to during this period become so memorable and beloved.
lines.cn: 这两点也许都能解释：为什么我们在这个时期听的歌曲会如此难忘、如此受喜爱。

lines.t: So there's nothing wrong with your parents because they don't like your music.
lines.cn: 所以你的父母不喜欢你的音乐，没什么不对。

lines.t: Rather, it's all part of the natural order of things.
lines.cn: 相反，这本就是事物自然秩序的一部分。
